summary: Frontend-only verification of the /login React crash bug ('Objects are not valid as a React child') on SOCPilot AI. Reproduced all three invalid-input scenarios plus admin/analyst regressions. Bug is FIXED — no React error overlay in any case, toast shows a readable string in all three failure paths. Admin and analyst logins succeed; /offenses and /settings load cleanly.

Not fatal but pollutes console on every authenticated route. Likely an editor/instrumentation artifact (x-ve-dynamic span) that should not be rendered into <option>.

action_items: OPTIONAL: Clean up Layout.jsx select/option to remove the stray <span> child inside <option> that triggers a hydration console warning on every authenticated page (unrelated to the login bug, but noisy).
critical_code_review_comments: api.js interceptor correctly flattens FastAPI 422 detail array/object into a string before rejecting — good defensive fix.
auth.jsx login() catch also handles array/object detail as belt-and-suspenders — good.
LoginPage.jsx passes r.error (guaranteed string now) into toast.error — safe.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Login 422-detail-array bug is confirmed fixed via axios response interceptor in /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js. Note that <input type='email'> in LoginPage triggers HTML5 validation which blocks fully-empty submits at the browser layer; during testing the type was flipped to 'text' via JS to force the 422 code path — verifying the interceptor. Under normal user behavior the browser-level validation catches empty/invalid before hitting the API, which is also fine. A separate benign hydration warning exists in Layout.jsx (<span> inside <option>).
rca of the issue: FastAPI returned 422 with `detail` as an array of Pydantic ErrorDetails objects. LoginPage passed `error.response.data.detail` directly into toast.error / rendered it as a child, causing React 'Objects are not valid as a React child'. Fix: axios response interceptor in /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js now stringifies array/object `detail` (joins x.msg with '; ') before rejection; auth.jsx login() catch also converts. Confirmed no crash across empty, invalid-format, and wrong-credential cases.
